name: What Should I Do if My Kitchen Floor Is Uneven After Cabinet Installation?

mainEntity.name: Should flooring be leveled before cabinets are installed during a kitchen renovation?
mainEntity.text: Should flooring be leveled before cabinets are installed during a kitchen renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Uneven floors are common in older homes and can create problems that become visible only after cabinets and countertops are installed. Cabinet boxes must be leveled and secured, but excessive shimming may create unsupported areas, inconsistent toe kicks, appliance clearance problems, or countertop issues. Ask the contractor to measure floor variation across the entire cabinet footprint before demolition or fabrication. The proposed solution may involve substrate repair, self-leveling material, localized patching, flooring replacement, or a planned installation sequence. Confirm whether flooring runs beneath cabinets, stops at cabinet edges, or must be installed after them; the correct approach depends on the material, manufacturer requirements, and design. Check refrigerator, dishwasher, range, and island clearances against the final floor height. Require the contract to state who handles floor leveling, transitions, baseboard removal, and color matching. Photograph the floor before installation and inspect cabinet level before countertops are templated. Do not accept uneven cabinets as a cosmetic issue if they affect appliance fit, doors, stone seams, or long-term support.
acceptedAnswer.description: The floor condition should be evaluated before cabinet installation because uneven surfaces can affect cabinet level, countertop seams, appliance fit, toe kicks, and doors. Depending on the flooring and cabinet plan, the contractor may level the substrate, install flooring in a defined sequence, or use approved shimming methods. Document the method before work starts.
